changes: 🔧 **Clearer message when a non-administrator signs in.** Only Orcanos administrators can use the platform console. A correct Orcanos username and password from a user who is not an administrator now shows *Only Orcanos administrators can sign in* on the login page, instead of the generic *Invalid credentials*.

✨ **The infrastructure handbook is now inside the console.** A new *Handbook* item in the sidebar shows the Orcanos AI infrastructure deck — apps, hosting, tenancy, residency, security, cost and next steps — updated for everything shipped since 10 September. Use the arrow keys to move, M for the index, or open it full screen.

✨ **Open Ask Paul or Traceability straight from the accounts list.** Each row has an Ask Paul ↗ and a Traceability ↗ button that opens the product in a new tab, at the US or EU address that matches the account's data region. Ask Paul has no EU deployment yet, so its button is disabled on EU accounts.

✨ **Every open ISO 27001 control now has a priority.** Procedure gaps (a policy, an inventory entry, a signed agreement) are Low; security gaps are Low, Medium, High or Critical depending on the finding. Filter by priority, or sort the list so the most urgent come first.
✨ **Each control tells you how to fix it.** The table shows the main recommendation, and the control's dialog lists the concrete steps for every open finding.

🐛 **A brief network hiccup between the console and Traceability no longer blanks its columns.** A dropped or timed-out connection is retried once before the accounts list gives up on the Traceability half.

🐛 **When Traceability really cannot be reached, the warning says which region and why** — for example "the connection timed out" on the EU instance — instead of a bare "fetch failed" that always showed the US address.

✨ **The Disaster recovery screen now explains each problem.** A "What needs attention" panel lists every issue found, which projects it affects, what the risk is and the steps to take. Click a flagged row for the same explanation for that project.
✨ **The ISO 27001 screen now covers Ask Paul and Traceability separately** — pick the system at the top; each has its own controls, runs and answers.
✨ **Every audit run is kept.** Import a run's ledger file from the screen, then switch between past runs to see what each one found, with the controls that changed since the run before marked.
✨ **Your answers have a history.** Save a comment without closing a control, or mark it resolved; every save is kept with who wrote it and when, and shown in the control's dialog.

✨ **BOM is a new module you can license per account** — a BOM pill on the accounts list, a BOM tick on the Traceability tab and on the create form, and its state on the account overview. It is off for every account until you turn it on, so customers do not see it.

🔒 **A BOM licence is never reported as saved when it was not** — on a traceability instance older than 3.46.0 the BOM switch is disabled and the server refuses the write, instead of the instance quietly dropping it.

✨ **A new Disaster recovery screen shows backup status for every account's database**, read live from Supabase's own point-in-time recovery — whether it's enabled, when the last backup completed, and which projects need attention. Status only for now: nothing here triggers a backup or a restore yet.

🔒 **Two accounts can no longer end up with the same name.** The create form and the API already refused a duplicate, but both check the list and then write — and when a database is being provisioned those two moments are minutes apart, so a second create for the same name could slip through in between. The name is now reserved by the database itself, without regard to case, so the last word belongs to the one place that cannot be raced.

🔒 **Creating an account whose provisioning is already running is refused, and says so.** Previously the name looked free until the job finished, because the account row is only written at the very end — a second attempt would start a second database for a name that could then never be saved.

✨ **A provisioning job that loses the race now fails with an explanation instead of a database error**, naming the Supabase project it created so it can be attached to the existing account or removed rather than quietly billed.

✨ **The account window is now one tab per system, not one per table.** Ask Paul and traceability are two different applications, and their settings were interleaved by where each value happened to be stored — Ask Paul's licence sat inside Traceability, while its database and on/off switch sat under “Account & databases”. There are now six tabs: Overview, Orcanos, Traceability, **Ask Paul**, **LLM** and Spend, each one thing you can think about without knowing the storage layout.

✨ **A new LLM tab shows both AI configurations together** — traceability's own provider, model and key, and the Ask Paul key that drives QMS AI's chat. They were at opposite ends of the window, which made it easy to miss that a customer runs one model in one app and something else in the other.

✨ **Spend now holds both ledgers.** The traceability AI cost used to be at the bottom of a settings dialog, where nobody looks for a number. The two stay listed separately rather than summed — one is a lifetime counter, the other a total over the events shown, so a combined figure would mean nothing.

✨ **Moving an account to another region is behind a button.** It happens once in an account's life, if ever, and it was the largest block on the first tab you land on — a red warning and a type-the-name box, making a routine screen look dangerous and the actual danger look ordinary.

✨ **Delete moved to the Ask Paul tab, where it says what it destroys**, and is collapsed until asked for. It removes the master account record — the Ask Paul account, its database credentials, its key and its sign-in methods — and never touches the traceability tenant, a distinction the old Danger zone on Overview did not draw.

📝 **The direct SQL Server section now says what it is for.** It is a read-only connection to the customer's own Orcanos database, and nothing on the platform reads it — both apps go through the Orcanos REST API instead. It is collapsed when empty and labelled, rather than looking like a required step that was skipped.

📝 **The Orcanos tab shows which tenant the API URL resolves to**, and warns when there is no URL and the tenant is being guessed from the account name — that tenant is what every module licence is keyed on.

✨ **A region move now shows its progress while it runs.** The seven steps appear as soon as the confirmation is typed — so the plan is readable before the move is authorised — and each one is ticked off as the server passes it, with the row counts it actually moved. Previously the button said "Moving…" for several minutes and reported everything only at the end. There is no percentage bar: the export, import and purge are each a single call to a regional instance that reports no fraction, and an invented bar on an operation that ends in a delete invites someone to decide it is stuck and reload.

🐛 **The account window's tabs are no longer clipped.** On a tab whose content was taller than the window, the tab strip was squeezed to a sliver — labels cut in half, with a scrollbar of their own. The strip now keeps its height and the tab content scrolls, as intended.

✨ **One screen per account** — click the account name and everything about it is in one window, as tabs: overview, account and databases, traceability, spend. The row used to offer a different set of buttons depending on facts you could not see, and a traceability-only tenant had no way in at all. A capability an account does not have is now a disabled tab that says why.

✨ **The data region is on the list** — a column on every row, read from the traceability instance that actually holds the data rather than from what was recorded. When the record and the instance disagree the row is flagged as a conflict, because one of them is wrong and nothing here can tell which.

✨ **A customer can be moved between regions** — from the account screen. Everything travels, the source copy is deleted only after both sides' row counts match, and the move is confirmed by typing the tenant name. It says up front that everyone signed in gets signed out, and that an Ask Paul vector database cannot move with it.
⚠️ **Deleting an account now needs you to type DELETE** — the old confirmation was a single click, one row away from a module toggle.

🔒 **Each region's traceability instance now has its own admin password** — `TRACE_ADMIN_PASSWORD` stays the US one, `TRACE_ADMIN_PASSWORD_EU` is the EU one. The two databases never travel together, so a single password covering both would have meant one leak opening both regions' admin APIs. A region counts as configured only when it has both a URL and its own password; there is no fallback to the other region's.

✨ **An account now has a data region, chosen when it is created** — United States or European Union. It decides which Supabase region the account's own database is created in and which traceability instance holds its data, so an EU customer's data can be kept in the EU for GDPR. Every existing account is recorded as United States, which is where it already is.

⚠️ **The region cannot be changed after the account is created** — and the account editor refuses the change rather than accepting it quietly. Neither a Supabase project nor a traceability volume can be moved between regions, so rewriting the value would move no data; it would only record the account as living somewhere it does not. Moving a customer means creating them again in the right region and migrating their data.

🔄 **The console now talks to one traceability instance per region** — the account list reads every configured region, and each licence change, AI setting, usage read and deletion is sent to the instance that actually holds that tenant. A region that cannot be reached makes the list say so, instead of showing its tenants as absent.

🔒 **Creating an EU account is refused while no EU traceability instance is configured** — it would have written the tenant's data to the United States while recording it as EU, and nothing anywhere would have reported the contradiction.

✨ **A new account is signposted in every region** — so a customer who opens the wrong region's address is redirected to their own instead of being told the account does not exist. The signpost is a tenant name and a region, nothing more, and it grants no access; if a region cannot be reached the account is still created and the console says which one to retry.
✨ **The account editor shows the data region, read-only** — it is fixed when the account is created, so it is displayed as a fact rather than offered as a field.

✨ **The console is usable on a phone.** The sidebar becomes a hamburger drawer under 860px, page headers and toolbars stack, the primary button spans the row, tables scroll horizontally rather than blowing out the viewport, and modals go full-screen so their body actually scrolls.
🔄 **Inputs are 16px on mobile** so iOS Safari stops zooming on focus, and the small pill buttons the account rows use have tap targets big enough for a thumb.

🐛 **The viewport meta was missing** — without it mobile browsers render at a 980px desktop viewport and the CSS breakpoints below never fire, so previous 'mobile' styling was invisible on any real phone.

🔄 **The Orcanos URL on the sign-in screen is now fixed, not typed** — the box shows the server this deployment checks passwords against and is disabled. It was free text so that a tenant other than the configured one could be reached; nobody needs to choose it here, and a value remembered from a previous sign-in could quietly pin the wrong server on that browser with no way to clear it.

🐛 **A tenant missing from traceability is no longer a dead end** — clicking Traceability or Training on an account that has no traceability entry now creates one, licensed for that module alone. Until now the pill refused, and the only way to add the entry was on the traceability instance's own admin page.

🐛 **Every new account gets its traceability entry, even with no module ticked** — the entry is what lets a tenant sign in at all, so skipping it left the account unreachable there and unfixable from this console. It is created licensed for nothing, one click away from being useful.

✨ **The create form shows which traceability tenant the licences will be written to** — taken from the Orcanos API URL, or guessed from the account name when there is none. The guess is now flagged as a guess: a licence keyed on the wrong tenant reaches nobody.
🔄 **A module pill with no licence on record says so** — its tooltip read “not licensed”, which is a decision somebody made; a dash means no answer from the source, which is not.

✨ **A duplicate account name is caught while you type** — the name is checked against every account and tenant already on the list, so the clash is shown under the field instead of after the whole form is filled in. The server still refuses one either way.

✨ **Ask Paul cannot be activated without a database** — it is the only module with a per-tenant database, and licensing it without one produced a hand-off into an app with nothing behind it. Blocked on all four controls that switch it on: the create form, the list pill, the traceability dialog and the account editor's Active switch, each refused by its own route as well. Turning it off is never blocked.

🔄 **An account created without a database starts Inactive** — Active is Ask Paul's switch and nothing else reads it, so an account with nowhere to read from must not start with half of it on. Adding the Vector DB details unlocks the switch in the same save.

🐛 **Modules ticked on the create form were dropped when a database was provisioned** — only the no-database path ever wrote them. They now travel with the job and are applied once the account row exists.

🐛 **Creating an account without a database failed** — the insert left out four columns the accounts table requires, so it was rejected with a not-null violation. 0.3.0's whole point did not work; this is the fix.
✨ **Create an account without a database** — pick the modules it is licensed for and the account exists immediately. Only Ask Paul needs a per-tenant database; Traceability and Training never did.
✨ **Modules chosen at creation** — Traceability, Training and Ask Paul are ticked on the create form and written to the tenant licence row, instead of being set afterwards one pill at a time.

🐛 **Provisioning could never succeed on Vercel** — the schema step dials `db.<ref>.supabase.co`, which has no IPv4 address, so it failed with a DNS error after creating a real billable project. Provisioning is now opt-in and off by default, and the form says what it costs.
✨ **Version in the footer** — the sidebar now shows the running version; click it for the release notes.
✨ **Release notes** — this file, plus a long-form changelog in `docs/changelog/CHANGELOG-v0.md`.
🔄 **CLAUDE.md trimmed** — ten releases of inline history moved to the changelog, leaving the current-version block and a pointer.
🔄 **Orcanos hosts only** — sign-in URLs are now restricted to `orcanos.com` and its subdomains by default, which is what makes the free-text URL box safe.
🐛 **Wrong Orcanos identity** — the platform admin row still carried test data, so every password was being checked against the wrong Orcanos user.
✨ **Choose the Orcanos server** — the sign-in screen now has an Orcanos URL field, remembered per browser.
✨ **A real default** — `ORCANOS_LOGIN_URL` (`app.orcanos.com/orcanos`); an unset `orcanos_api_url` used to be a 500.
🔄 **Richer login audit** — every sign-in event records which Orcanos server answered, and whether the caller chose it.
✨ **Sign in by username** — the first field now accepts an Orcanos user name as well as an email address.
✨ **Show/hide password** — a toggle on the password field.
🗑️ **Microsoft sign-in withdrawn** — it trusted an email attribute an attacker can set in their own tenant; off in code, not just hidden.
🔄 **Google and Orcanos sign-in unaffected** — each method resolves independently.
🗑️ **Status column removed** — it was never a platform gate; an account set Inactive could still sign in to traceability.
🔄 **Ask Paul writes both halves** — one pill now sets the master flag and the traceability licence, and ANDs them for display.
🔄 **Security audit and hardening** — full review of the tree, recorded in `SECURITY_AUDIT_2026-08-29.md`.
🐛 **SSRF guard gaps** — IPv4-mapped IPv6 spellings of loopback walked past the address check; CGNAT space is now blocked too.
🐛 **Console was framable** — security headers added, chiefly `frame-ancestors 'none'`.
🐛 **Google sign-in now requires `email_verified`** — the email domain is half the platform gate.
✨ **Orcanos mark** — the logo now appears on the sidebar brand and the login card.
🔄 **QMS AI pill is now Ask Paul** — and reads the real licence column instead of being derived from account status.
🐛 **Version mismatch** — `package.json` said 0.1.1 while the docs said 0.2.0.
✨ **Orcanos-backed sign-in** — email sign-in verifies the password through Orcanos `QW_Login` instead of a stored hash.
🐛 **Tenant pin corrected** — it compared against the config-row label rather than the account's real Orcanos tenant segment.
🐛 **Google sign-in fixed** — first live run against the master database; two never-applied migrations found.
